editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin 'In monasterio Lutrensi, in Burgundia' is Lure, in Burgundy, not Brittany.

mr:0130-theophilus-iuvenis.note: The unofficial English 2004 edition renders the cognomen as "the Youth" (Latin cognoménto Iúvenis, Italian (CEI) detto il Giovane); "the Younger" is the conventional English epithet, which the English subject follows.

mr:0212-antonius-caulea.note: The unofficial English 2004 edition dates him "under Emperor Leo III the Isaurian"; the Latin print has Leónis imperatóris Sexti and the Italian (CEI) Leone VI: the emperor is Leo VI the Wise.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin is Antoninus, not Antonius (Anthony).

mr:0217-septem-fundatores-servorum-maria.note: On this day the 1749 edition prints the eulogy of Alexius Falconieri alone, one of the seven founders; the 2004 edition commemorates the seven founders together. The historical eulogy is kept under this ID.

mr:0323-rebecca-de-himlaya.note: Plain entry (11., no asterisk) in the Latin editio altera 2004 print, visually verified on the page scan; the Italian (CEI) edition marks the entry with an asterisk.

mr:0410-beda.note: The unofficial English 2004 edition mistranslates the subject as "Saint Peter the Younger"; the Latin print has sancti Bedæ iunióris and the Italian (CEI) san Beda il Giovane. The English subject follows the Latin.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin has 'Episcopi et Confessoris', not a martyr.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin has 'Maximini' (Maximinus of Trier), but the English says 'Maximus'.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1749: This text joins the opening of Privatus's eulogy to the body of the eulogy of Paternus of Fondi (mr:0821-paternus): a line has evidently dropped. The 1914 English prints both eulogies.

mr:0103-cyrinus-et-socii.note: The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to the sole Theogenes

mr:0114-triginta-octo-monachi-montis-sin.note: 2004 merged the Sinai (38) and Raithu (43) monks into one eulogy, so the Sinai eulogy may be same_eulogy with mr:0114-monachi-raithi; alternatively keep as its own deprecated ID. [Same-day: proposed as a merge, since only renamed celebrations get a same-day same_eulogy link.] [Not a merge: both historical editions print the two eulogies separately on this day, so each keeps its own ID.]

mr:0114-euphrasius-africae.note: The historical editions commemorate a bishop Euphrasius in Africa on this day; the 2004 edition's eulogy of the day is Euphrasius, bishop of Clermont (mr:0114-euphrasius). The two are keyed apart and linked as the same eulogy, whose subject the 2004 edition changed.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: "Whose birthday is the 7th of this month" seems to be an error, as this would point to Canute Lavard (mr:0107-canutus-lavard), who was not a king.

mr:0123-agathangelus.note: The 2004 eulogy mr:0123-clemens-et-agathangelus joins Clement and Agathangelus; the historical editions give Agathangelus a separate line. Partial overlap; link rather than merge. [Same-day: proposed as a merge, since only renamed celebrations get a same-day same_eulogy link.] [Not a merge: both historical editions print the two eulogies separately on this day, so each keeps its own ID.]

mr:0205-genuinus-et-albuinus.note: The 1914 English fuses the eulogies of Ingenuinus and Albuinus of Brixen, which the 1749 edition and the 2004 edition print separately (mr:0205-ingenuinus, mr:0205-albuinus); it is linked to both.

mr:0214-valentinus-interamnae.note: 2004 has a single Valentine (via Flaminia), generally identified with the bishop of Terni; but 1749/1914 print both eulogies the same day, so a merge would put two historical eulogies on one ID — a same_eulogy link may be preferable. [Not a merge: both historical editions print the two eulogies separately on this day, so each keeps its own ID.]

mr:0220-eleutherius-et-socii.note: The 1749 edition names Eleutherius, bishop, and 128 others in Persia on February 20; probably the eulogy of Sadoth, bishop, and 128 companions (mr:0218-sadoth-et-socii): same place, king (Sapor), number and refusal to adore the sun (#47).

mr:0504-triginta-novem-martyres-phaenoni.note: The 1749 and 1914 editions print the thirty-nine martyrs of the mines of Phaeno as a eulogy of their own, after that of Silvanus of Gaza; the 2004 edition commemorates them together with him in mr:0504-silvanus-et-socii.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: 'Lucius' where the Latin has 'Mucii'.

mr:0813-hippolytus.note: The legendary Hippolytus buried in the Ager Veranus is traditionally the same Hippolytus as the 2004 Pontian-and-Hippolytus eulogy. But the 2004 eulogy leads with Pontian and is a rewritten narrative, so a merge is doubtful.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: This text is the rewritten eulogy of the Twelve Brothers of Benevento and does not name Donatus or Felix; it succeeds the 1749 eulogy, which mentions the twelve brothers' feast and Benevento, but its subject differs.

mr:0905-quinctius-et-socii.note: The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to Quintus alone (mr:0905-quintus, see #52).

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: This text joins the Octave and the Seven Sorrows in one sentence, with no clean point to split it; the Seven Sorrows half corresponds to mr:0915-maria-perdolens.
Translation error: the 1749 Latin calls him 'Episcopi Abrincensis et Confessoris', not a martyr.

mr:0928-marcus-et-socii.note: The 2004 edition drops Mark and leads with the three brothers.

editions.martyrologium_romanum_1914_en_unofficial: Translation error: the Latin is a translation of relics (Translatio), not a birthday.

mr:1030-maximus-apameae.note: The historical editions place Maximus at Apamea, 2004 at Cumae: keyed apart and matched, as Euphrasius on 0114.
